name: Hamel Recreation Center
use: Student recreation and fitness center (former Snively Arena); part of the Key Auto Group Complex
builtText: 1965 as Snively Arena; renovated, expanded and renamed 1995; expanded 2016–17
architect: 2016–17 expansion: Hughes Group Architects (builder Shawmut Design and Construction)

renovations.what: Renovated and expanded; renamed for benefactor Dana Hamel
About 100,000 sq ft expansion and renovation with replacement of the outdoor pool; $5.5M of the $35.5M project went to deferred maintenance (roof, air handlers, hardwood floors)

facts.text: Built in 1965 as Snively Arena, named for coach A. Barr 'Whoop' Snively; home of UNH men's hockey until the Whittemore Center opened in 1995.
The 2016–17 expansion added fitness space, a one-tenth-mile suspended track, wellness space, an instructional kitchen and a large multi-activity court.
Most of the $30 million non-maintenance cost was financed by a loan repaid by students.
Since 2023 it forms the Key Auto Group Complex with the Whittemore Center; UNH describes it as 158,000 sq ft with 18,000 sq ft of fitness space.

verdict: Snively Arena's 1965 vault wrapped by a 2017 stone-and-glass addition: a big, bright, well-used rec centre students paid for.
notes: Old row's exact areas (98,920 sf renovation + 69,930 sf addition) and 'Living Wall / Sculptural Forest Wall' interior descriptions come from architect pages I could not open (Athletic Business returned 403); not re-verified. Archives say '100,000 square foot expansion and renovation' and date it 2016; TNH says the renovated building would be usable spring 2017. Old row's 86%-usage stat not re-verified. Wikipedia's article title is 'Hamel Recreation Center' (URL redirects from Snively_Arena). Photos: 1965 arena is a white barrel-vaulted shell; the new entry (Flickr, 2018) is a tall stone-and-glass block with a projecting louvred glass bay and canopy; MAC West courts have high open-truss ceilings. Licensed photos: 2021 (Ken Gallager) and 2018 (Flickr CC BY) show the 2017 entrance addition: buff stone piers, a projecting louvered glass bay, metal panel wings and large windows, with the white 1965 arena vault behind. Crisp and contemporary.
judgeNotes: Photos show a crisp but generic entrance pavilion; interior reference shows bright courts. Exterior up a point from the old run now that the addition is visible.
